A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TURN research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite pagination and presentation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original MATH and MBPP evaluations, temperature-selection analyses, and stochastic-process simulations, including results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original evaluations and simulations, including model-level results, sampling-variance measurements, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 is identical. TURN retains entropy-curve estimation, turning-point selection, and adaptation factors of 0 for majority voting and 0.1 for best-of-N. The stochastic-process update rules also remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use MATH, MBPP, and the same synthetic simulation scenarios. MATH best-of-N calibration remains in Appendix C. Figure 1's OpenMath2 example was already represented in v1's Appendix D.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons retain the same fixed temperatures from 0.1 to 1.1 in increments of 0.2, grid-search optima, and TURN without aggregation adaptation. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain 200 MATH problems, 100 MBPP problems, 256 generated samples per question and temperature, evaluation at sample size 128, and the same metrics and sampling settings. The appendix equation edit does not establish a changed experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The greedy-generation control, aggregation-adaptation analysis, sample-budget sensitivity, and simulation noise-tolerance analyses are retained. Appendix plots and supporting analyses are unchanged; Figure 1 redisplays an existing model example.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2.1 changes averaging over '500 samples' to '500 seeds', making seed-level replication explicit without establishing additional runs. Table 3 retains its 50-trial variance analysis; 'trails' becomes 'trials'.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the appendix plots retain their results. Table 1's added 92.3% and 84.6% labels restate the existing hit rates of 12/13 and 11/13. Figure 1's replacement curve was already reported in Figure 14.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1.7 expands the entropy definition but introduces a sign inconsistency: the new expression H = (1/K) sum p log p lacks the minus sign retained in its following expansion. v1's expression had the correct negative sign. Other definitions and update rules remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: automatic near-optimal temperature selection without labeled validation data, advantages over fixed temperatures, and entropy-based interpretation supported by a stochastic model.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1.5 removes the assertion that high-probability improper tokens will be selected regardless of temperature. Their exclusion from the simulation remains, but its stated rationale is revised. The main interpretations and applicability claims are retained.

D1.justification: Software, hardware, inference settings, model links, and code-access information remain the same. The TURN repository link moves from the first-page footnote to the abstract; this is not newly provided access.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning against previous temperature-selection approaches remain unchanged. The Yi-coder reference receives a different URL but retains the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, especially in Appendix B, adds acknowledgments, updates publication information, and relocates the code link. The substantive section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with clearer annotations, revised axes, and an existing OpenMath2 example replacing Llemma. Table 1 is enlarged and relocated, with percentage hit-rate headings. Captions, table labels, spacing, and page flow receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 improves Figure 1's explanatory annotations, Table 1's readability, and disclosure of the simulation's 500 seeds. However, it introduces an internally inconsistent entropy equation in Appendix B.1.7. With the method and empirical evidence otherwise unchanged, these limited presentation and reporting gains versus the new mathematical defect leave the net quality direction unclear.
